solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thrashing killer whale almost does for range rover?

indicators.note: thrashing about suggests wild movement, so the letters are churned into a new order
almost means the last letter of the word whale is dropped

explanation.surface: A killer whale thrashing about in the water nearly finishes off someone roaming the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims WHALE to WHAL, which joins KILLER as the anagram fodder; 'does for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler who roams over a range of hills is literally a rover of ranges.

clue.text: That one's local shrub

parts.note: that one means a male person, he
in local dialect speech 'is' can come out as 'be', as in 'he be'

explanation.surface: A pointer to a particular bush that grows in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' signals regional dialect, where 'he is' becomes 'he be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen flowering bushes popular in gardens, many from New Zealand.

clue.text: Failed to include Chinese, perhaps, in report of milk production

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: failed to include means lacked, and a Chinese person is, for example, Asian: lacked Asian

explanation.surface: A news report on a dairy's output that left out a Chinese contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'lacked Asian' runs together into the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactation is the biological process of secreting milk from mammary glands.

clue.text: West's game fine

parts.note: I spy is a children's guessing game

explanation.surface: A Western sport or pastime declared to be perfectly all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Wispy hair or cloud is fine and thin, slight in texture.

clue.text: Kings and queens changing sides at first don't show it

definitions.text: Kings and queens changing sides at first don't show it

indicators.note: the opening letter swaps one side for the other, right becoming left

parts.note: kings and queens collectively are royalty

explanation.surface: Monarchs who switch allegiance are not displaying faithfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the start is replaced by L (left); the whole clue then describes turncoat monarchs who lack the quality named.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness or allegiance is exactly what monarchs who change sides fail to display.

clue.text: Wapping boss maybe to 'urry in 'ere?

indicators.note: in places the hurrying inside the editor

parts.note: Wapping housed national newspaper offices, so its boss might be an editor, ED
to hurry is to hasten; dropping the H Cockney-style leaves ASTEN

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks whether the newspaper chief will rush over to their part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is in London's East End, home to Cockneys who drop their H's, so 'ere' (here) is the answer for the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is the part of East London, including Wapping, where Cockney speakers would call it here.

clue.text: Couple with little one delay getting married

indicators.note: delay means the letter for married is held back, arriving later in the word

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A pair with a small child decide to postpone their wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: MITE with its M moved from the front to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are informally called an item.

clue.text: Note pulse rising and falling?

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
dal is a pulse, a lentil or split pea

explanation.surface: Remark on a heartbeat that goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's tides go up and down, so anything moving that way is a playful description of the word.

clue.text: You can get chips with this Asian money when converted

definitions.text: You can get chips with this

indicators.note: converted money changes form, so these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Changing Asian currency lets you buy gambling chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests casino tokens bought with converted money, but they are fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a common dip or sauce served alongside fried potato chips.

clue.text: Paul came out to make a confession

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are put into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A man called Paul came out, an admission about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'my fault', an acknowledgement of one's guilt.

clue.text: Foreign money upsets county

definitions.meaning: dollars, from a British view foreign currency, are informally called this
a horse that throws its rider does this
short form of Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London

explanation.surface: Overseas currency throws a shire into disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: slang for dollars, a verb for unseating a rider, and an abbreviated English shire.

clue.text: Indeed it's true — daughter retired, turning in some hours ago

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the other two words

parts.note: indeed, as an affirmative, means yes
ay (aye) is an affirmative meaning it's true

indicators.note: turning means D and RET are read backwards

explanation.surface: Confirming that a girl went to bed after twisting and turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like going to bed but is the abbreviation; 'turning' makes TERD, which sits 'in' the two affirmatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today ended some hours back, a loose but fair paraphrase.

clue.text: How goods may be taken back, blouse oddly lacking colour

indicators.note: back means those two words are read in reverse

parts.note: goods may be transported by van

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of blouse are missing, leaving its second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Instructions for returning a blouse that came in the wrong shade.
explanation.walkthrough: BY VAN reversed gives NAVYB, then L, U, E come from blouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark shade of blue, named after naval uniforms.

clue.text: Cause of stoppage in food processing sector

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark that makes a reader pause
the large intestine, part of the digestive tract

explanation.surface: A strike halts a factory section that processes food.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark creating a pause, and the bowel section where digested food is processed.

clue.text: Heads for extreme sports gym, clutching a training shoe

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of the two following words
clutching means the gym letters hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
drill is training by repeated exercises

explanation.surface: Kit for extreme-sports enthusiasts heading to the gym, carrying a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sandal-style footwear with a rope sole.

clue.text: Wake up kids for dinner?

parts.note: to stir is to wake from sleep
fry are young fish, by extension small children

explanation.surface: A call to rouse the children for the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of quickly fried chopped food, one example of an evening meal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Blend beer, mostly, in main part of crate

parts.note: to fuse is to blend together

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Mixing beer, chiefly, within the bulk of a crate of bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crate' is slang for an old aircraft, not a box of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of an aircraft, which slang calls a crate, is its main structure.

clue.text: Call on Miss Woodhouse to get rid of a problem

indicators.note: on means placed next to, the second piece following the first
to get rid of means the letter A is removed

parts.note: to dial is to call by telephone
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: Visiting Emma Woodhouse to dispose of a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAL + EMMA gives DIALEMMA; removing the A from DIAL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult choice between alternatives is a predicament.

clue.text: Sucker getting directions just before end, being close

indicators.note: the new letters go in immediately ahead of the final letter

parts.note: muggins is a fool or dupe, a sucker
E and S are compass directions, east and south

explanation.surface: A dupe gets told the way shortly before the finish, and it is nearly over.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggy, humid weather is described as close; the noun names that heavy, airless state.

clue.text: Little woman keeping home gets big let-off

indicators.note: keeping means holding the home word inside

parts.note: Amy is one of the sisters in Little Women
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A small lady staying in the house gets away with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' is Amy March from Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon for offences is a large-scale release from punishment.

clue.text: Did long November come early within accounting period?

indicators.note: come early means the N moves to an earlier spot within the word

parts.note: a year end closes a company's accounting period
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Was November extended by arriving ahead of time in the financial year?
explanation.walkthrough: In YEAREND the N jumps ahead of the E; 'within' says the move stays inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn, so 'did long' is the past tense of that wish.

clue.text: Let rip on accelerator — that'll clear the road!

parts.note: to tear is to let rip, to rush
the gas is the accelerator pedal of a car

explanation.surface: A motorist floors the pedal to scatter traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The motoring picture misleads: riot police use the answer to disperse crowds from a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this irritant to disperse crowds, clearing the street.

clue.text: Blasts heads of Internet Explorer for juvenile digital item

parts.note: toots are blasts on a horn

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A web browser complaint about a children's computer gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' means relating to fingers and toes, not computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish word for a toe, and toes are digits, so a little digit.

clue.text: Have fun in bar after retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lever is a bar used for prising

explanation.surface: Enjoying oneself in a pub once one has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry, celebrate noisily.

clue.text: Plant to check and check

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
CH is the chess notation abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A mole or spy is placed to keep doubly close watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing legume of the pea family grown as fodder.

clue.text: Scented an instant reaction from Italian team?

parts.note: Roma is the football club AS Roma
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Something with a smell provokes an immediate reaction from Italian players.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a strong pleasant smell, fragrant.

clue.text: Perhaps one from Ayr racecourse

parts.note: a means one
a person from Ayr, a Scottish town, is a Scot

explanation.surface: A spectator maybe from Ayr at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a native of Ayr is just one example of a Scot. Ayr itself has a racecourse, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous horse-racing venue in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Lech Walesa governed without majorities on left and right

indicators.text: without majorities on left and right
indicators.note: the bulk of each word is removed from both ends, leaving only its central pair

explanation.surface: A Polish leader ruled without a parliamentary majority on either wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lech' looks like Wałęsa's first name but is the verb to lust. WALESA leaves LE, GOVERNED leaves ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To lech is to look lustfully, which is what a lascivious look does.

clue.text: They are in case of nasty sting with tail

indicators.note: nasty suggests something twisted and spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scorpion-like creature with a painful sting in its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is a lawsuit, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties in a lawsuit are involved in a legal case.

clue.text: Church's representative entering cloth

indicators.note: entering means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church's delegate going into a room wearing clerical cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A light fabric with a wrinkled surface.

clue.text: Screech owl's repeated call

indicators.note: 's stands for has, the two words containing the answer within them

explanation.surface: The cry of a screech owl comes again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound reflected back is a call heard a second time.

clue.text: One using time during break returned to do exams again after having raved excessively

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece following the anagram
raving excessively suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged
returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to resit is to take exams again

explanation.surface: A student back from a break repeats exams after partying too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is a commercial break; the definition is a company buying airtime there.
explanation.definitionFit: A company promoting its products buys airtime in the commercial interval on television.
